THE COMPOSITION PARADIGM
Not a component library.
A composition system.

A resource catalogue gives you reusable building blocks. Tessellate adds a product brief, shared design settings, and a manifest that connects screens, resources, and project intent.

Starting from a Resource Catalogue
Choose resources: The product team decides which components belong on each screen.
Carry design decisions: Shared tokens and interaction patterns need to stay aligned across resources.
Connect the screens: The team defines navigation, content, and how interface parts work together.
Review generated code: Check markup, styles, and behavior in the context of the product.
Outcome: Resource choice, integration, and consistency remain with the product team.
Tessellate Composition Engine
Product model: Interprets a brief into a product domain, audience, and user jobs before planning screens.
Design DNA: Shared visual settings guide composition and apply to resources that support them.
Manifest audit: A 100-point rubric scores declared structure and resource metadata; it does not certify the rendered interface.
Validated mutations: Workbench and integration tools apply typed manifest changes while respecting locked scope.
Outcome: Export a standalone React + Tailwind project from the manifest you composed and reviewed.

INTERFACE MATHEMATICS
Compatibility scoring & normalisation.

Candidate resources are ranked against their declared metadata, role requirements, dependencies, and the project’s Design DNA. The score helps narrow choices; browser review still matters.

DNA Distance Vector

Compares normalized project Design DNA with a resource’s declared priors. The resulting fit score is one signal used to rank candidates.

Hard Constraint Gates

Role, variant, and dependency requirements can rule out candidates. Declared accessibility metadata still needs to be checked against the rendered interface.

Responsive Strategies

Resources declare responsive approaches. Review Workbench and exported previews at the widths your product needs; layout is not automatically substituted for you.

AGENT-NATIVE ARCHITECTURE
Built for autonomous agents and humans alike.

Coding agents and people can inspect the same project manifest and use the same typed mutation contracts to change an interface.

Project manifests: Export a composed project as a schema-validated .tess.json file.
Structured mutations: Typed operations can update project structure and provide inverse changes for undo.
Registered resources: Composition selects from the resource registry; unsupported roles remain visible for review.
Agent handoff: Exports the project brief, design, implementation, components, dependencies, and an agent prompt.

PUBLIC COMMONS
100% Free. No Pro component gates. No download caps.

Interface building blocks belong in the public commons. Tessellate will never lock high-value tables or charts behind a paywalled subscription. The entire component and pattern vocabulary is freely accessible to developers and autonomous agents forever.

CREATOR ECOSYSTEM
Publish resources with a declared contract.

Resource manifests can describe variants, slots, dependencies, and Design DNA priors. This helps compatible React tools inspect a resource before integration; each target application still needs its own review.

Learn how to author & submit a manifest
QUALITY & SECURITY INVARIANTS
Inspectable quality.
Verify in the browser.

The deterministic audit inspects manifest and declared resource metadata. Browser accessibility, visual behaviour and export builds require runtime verification.

Manifest Audit Rubric
Rubric: 100 points total
Cohesion
20 pts

Palette, curvature, and typography alignment

Accessibility
20 pts

Declared accessibility metadata and semantic roles

Performance
15 pts

Bundle size, dependencies, and runtime complexity

Responsive Layout
15 pts

Ergonomic scaling across mobile, tablet & desktop

Visual Hierarchy
10 pts

Clear focal headers & structural navigation

Density Consistency
5 pts

Controlled spacing variance between cards

Motion Consistency
5 pts

Cadence alignment & reduced-motion safety

Design Compliance
5 pts

Declared design constraints and compatibility

Interaction Harmony
5 pts

Clear single primary button actions per panel

Build and Runtime Budgets
Zero Runtime Lock-In: Exported code is vanilla React 19 + Tailwind CSS 4. No Tessellate SDK required in production.
Reduced-Motion First Class: Smooth degradation to static fades when the user prefers reduced motion.
Homepage script budget: Initial JavaScript is checked against a 150 KB gzip target. Load time depends on the device and connection.
WCAG 2.2 AA is a target. A metadata score does not certify accessibility; test the rendered project.
